name: Cameco Corporation

profile.description: Cameco Corporation is one of the world's largest uranium producers and a leading provider of nuclear fuel cycle services, operating through Uranium, Fuel Services, and Westinghouse segments. The company mines, mills, refines, converts, and fabricates uranium for nuclear power generation, and through its 49% stake in Westinghouse Electric Company (acquired 2023), provides nuclear reactor technology, maintenance, and engineering services globally. With TTM revenue of approximately $3.5B and a 10.2% profit margin, Cameco is headquartered in Saskatoon, Canada. Q1 2026 adjusted net earnings more than doubled YoY to C$203M ($0.47/share), driven by 15% uranium revenue growth to C$712M on higher volumes and prices [1].

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Cameco executed a transformative strategic pivot by acquiring a 49% stake in Westinghouse Electric Company in 2023 for approximately $4.5B, evolving from a pure-play uranium miner into an integrated nuclear fuel cycle company spanning mining through reactor technology and services [1]. This fundamentally repositioned Cameco in the nuclear value chain during a period of rising demand. Additionally, the company demonstrated strategic discipline by placing McArthur River — one of the world's largest high-grade uranium mines — on care-and-maintenance from 2018 to 2022, refusing to sell below long-term contract prices. AI Deployment (0/2): No evidence of AI deployment in customer-facing products or quantified internal AI-driven cost savings. The nuclear industry operates under strict regulatory frameworks that limit rapid technology deployment. Market Share (2/2): Cameco is the world's second-largest uranium producer behind Kazakhstan's Kazatomprom, with major operations at McArthur River/Key Lake and Cigar Lake in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin [1][3]. Through Westinghouse, Cameco now has a position in nuclear reactor technology serving approximately half the world's operating reactors. Product Pipeline (1/2): Cameco's pipeline includes expanded McArthur River production capacity, Westinghouse AP1000 and AP300 small modular reactor technology, and long-term contracts covering 28M+ lbs U3O8 annually for the next five years [1]. Timelines for SMR commercialization remain uncertain. R&D Intensity (0/1): R&D spending is modest relative to revenue, with most technology investment flowing through Westinghouse rather than Cameco directly. Below top quartile for the broader energy sector.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Cameco's stated purpose centers on 'safely and reliably providing clean nuclear energy to power a clean-air world,' connecting uranium production to the clean energy transition and climate goals [3]. The mission is specific to nuclear energy and differentiates from generic energy company statements, but it describes the industry's value proposition rather than a distinctive Cameco vision. Community Impact (1/2): Cameco maintains long-standing partnerships with northern Saskatchewan Indigenous communities, including employment and training programs, community investment agreements, and environmental monitoring programs [4]. The company is widely regarded as a responsible employer in remote communities. However, specific dollar amounts and program outcomes are not prominently disclosed. Employee Retention (1/2): CEO Tim Gitzel has led Cameco since 2011, providing 15 years of leadership stability. The 2025 AGM Board Chair remarks expressed 'tremendous confidence' in Gitzel and the senior management team [3]. Nuclear industry employees tend to have long tenures due to specialized skills and regulatory requirements. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of meaningful net insider buying by Gitzel or other executives. Insider transactions are not prominent in search results.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock on available metrics. Cameco's financial profile reflects a capital-intensive uranium mining and nuclear services business in a secular growth phase. D/E of 17.1% is well below the 70% target (score 1.0), reflecting a conservative balance sheet with $1.1B in cash against $1.2B in debt [1]. The 5-year revenue CAGR of approximately 18% (score 1.0, 2x weight) reflects both organic growth from uranium price recovery and the transformative Westinghouse acquisition. However, ROE of just 5.1% is well below the 15% target (score 0.34, 2x weight), reflecting the capital-intensive nature of mining and the early stage of Westinghouse integration [1]. Revenue declined 7.2% YoY in the most recent quarter due to lower planned deliveries and reduced Westinghouse equity earnings (score 0.43) [2]. Forward P/E of 43.1 is significantly above the 20 target (score 0.42), pricing in substantial future uranium price appreciation and Westinghouse earnings growth. Profit margin of 10.2% is below the 20% target (score 0.51). The Forward PEG of 1.92 falls between target and floor (score 0.54, 2x weight). Daily dollar volume of $250M provides strong liquidity.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (9/9): Cameco's core business — extracting uranium from underground mines, processing it into nuclear fuel, and providing nuclear reactor technology through Westinghouse — is structurally immune to AI disruption. AI cannot substitute for physical uranium, and nuclear power generation operates under rigorous regulatory frameworks (NRC, CNSC) that create insurmountable barriers to software-based disruption [1][3]. More importantly, AI is a direct demand catalyst for Cameco: AI data centers require enormous baseload electricity, driving renewed interest in nuclear power as the only scalable zero-carbon baseload source. Tech companies including Microsoft, Google, and Amazon have signed nuclear power purchase agreements, and over 30 countries pledged to triple nuclear capacity by 2050 at COP28. Cameco sits at the foundation of this supply chain. AI Opportunity (0/1): Cameco does not generate direct revenue from AI products or services. The company benefits from AI-driven electricity demand but does not sell AI technology.

infinite_game.summary: Cameco demonstrates strong infinite game characteristics through disciplined long-term decision-making, most notably the courageous choice to shut down McArthur River for four years (2018-2022) rather than sell uranium below sustainable prices, and the transformative Westinghouse acquisition that repositioned the company for the nuclear renaissance. CEO Gitzel's 15-year tenure provides leadership continuity. The company's commitment to safety and Indigenous community partnerships reflects values-driven operations. However, the company's competitive positioning is more about structural advantage in a capital-intensive industry than a deeply articulated Just Cause.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Cameco's purpose of powering a clean-air world through safe nuclear energy connects the company's work to the existential challenge of climate change and global energy access [3]. This purpose has been consistently articulated through the uranium price collapse of 2016-2020, guiding the decision to maintain production capacity rather than permanently close mines. The cause is genuine and connects to something bigger than profit. However, it reflects the nuclear industry's collective purpose rather than a uniquely Cameco vision, and the company has not demonstrated the kind of purpose-driven strategic sacrifice that earns a 3 in Sinek's framework.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Cameco demonstrates stable leadership under CEO Tim Gitzel (since 2011) with a management team the board describes as widely respected for their safety culture and operational competence [3]. The nuclear industry's regulatory requirements create a natural emphasis on safety culture and procedural discipline. However, the Westinghouse CEO resignation in early 2025 — requiring an interim replacement while a successor was recruited — introduces some uncertainty about integration culture [3]. No specific voluntary turnover data available.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Cameco acknowledges Kazatomprom's cost advantage as the world's largest uranium producer and uses this competitive dynamic to drive efficiency improvements at its own mines [3]. The company's strategic response to competitive pressure — investing in the Westinghouse acquisition to move up the value chain rather than competing solely on mining costs — reflects an infinite mindset of using rivals' strengths to improve rather than trying to destroy competitors.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The 2023 Westinghouse acquisition fundamentally changed Cameco's business model from a pure uranium miner to an integrated nuclear fuel cycle company, representing a significant strategic evolution [1]. However, the pivot was additive (acquiring a complementary business) rather than transformative (abandoning a core business). Cameco has not faced the existential test of having to walk away from its uranium mining heritage, and the Westinghouse deal was opportunistic rather than born of strategic necessity.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (2/2): Cameco demonstrated extraordinary courage by placing McArthur River — one of the world's premier uranium mines — on care-and-maintenance from 2018 to 2022, forgoing billions in potential revenue rather than selling uranium below prices that would sustain the long-term health of the industry [1][3]. This decision cost Cameco significant near-term earnings during a period when competitors continued producing. The company then doubled down with the $4.5B Westinghouse acquisition in 2023, betting heavily on the nuclear renaissance before the current wave of tech-company nuclear contracts validated the thesis. Both decisions exemplify choosing long-term capability over short-term earnings.

investment_thesis: Cameco at $80.51 with a $35B market cap is uniquely positioned at the intersection of the nuclear renaissance and AI-driven electricity demand. The company is the world's second-largest uranium producer with long-term contracts covering 28M+ lbs U3O8 annually, and its 49% Westinghouse stake provides exposure to nuclear reactor technology serving approximately half the world's operating fleet [1][2]. Q1 2026 adjusted net earnings more than doubled to C$203M ($0.47/share), with uranium revenue up 15% to C$712M. The structural demand thesis is compelling: AI data centers require enormous baseload electricity, tech companies are signing nuclear power purchase agreements, and 30+ countries pledged to triple nuclear capacity by 2050 at COP28. With a conservative D/E of 17%, $1.1B in cash, and 2026 production guidance of 19.5-21.5M lbs, Cameco offers leveraged exposure to the secular uranium bull market [1].
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on valuation, earnings volatility, and execution risk. At 43x forward earnings and 136x trailing earnings, Cameco prices in substantial uranium price appreciation and Westinghouse earnings growth that have not yet materialized [1][2]. Q2 2026 revenue fell 7% YoY with EPS declining 92% due to lower planned deliveries and reduced Westinghouse equity earnings, demonstrating the lumpiness of uranium sales and the early-stage nature of Westinghouse integration. ROE of just 5.1% on the current asset base is well below industrial targets, and profit margin of 10.2% reflects the capital intensity of mining operations. The uranium market faces potential supply increases from Kazakhstan's Kazatomprom and new African projects, and any delay in nuclear new-build timelines would undercut the long-duration demand thesis. The Westinghouse leadership transition (CEO resignation in early 2025) adds integration uncertainty, and Cameco's stock price at $80.51 sits near its 52-week low of $77.70, suggesting the market is already repricing the growth outlook [2][4].
key_catalysts: AI-driven nuclear power demand — tech companies (Microsoft, Google, Amazon) are signing multi-billion-dollar nuclear power purchase agreements for data center baseload electricity, directly driving uranium demand and long-term contracting at prices favorable to Cameco's production portfolio [1]

Westinghouse earnings inflection — the AP1000 reactor technology is the design of choice for new nuclear builds globally, and Westinghouse's installed base servicing business provides recurring revenue as the existing fleet extends operating licenses from 40 to 60 and potentially 80 years [1][3]

Uranium supply deficit — global uranium demand exceeds mine supply by approximately 40M+ lbs annually, drawing down secondary supplies and supporting prices above $80/lb, with Cameco's long-term contracts locking in prices through 2028+ [1]
key_risks: Extreme valuation at 43x forward earnings and 1.92x PEG prices in nuclear renaissance outcomes that remain speculative — actual nuclear new-build timelines historically experience multi-year delays and cost overruns, and any delay compresses the present value of Cameco's growth [1]

Earnings lumpiness and Q2 2026 weakness — uranium deliveries are concentrated in specific quarters under long-term contracts, creating volatile quarterly results that can mislead on underlying trends, as Q2 2026's 92% EPS decline demonstrated [2]

Westinghouse integration and leadership risk — the subsidiary's CEO resigned in early 2025, and the Westinghouse equity earnings already declined in H1 2026, raising questions about whether the $4.5B investment will generate the returns needed to justify Cameco's premium valuation [2][3]
